result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_balanced_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a balanced k-ary tree to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4638-L4798){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_balanced_tree( k, h, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Balanced tree](/assets/graphs/add-balanced-tree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three binary trees side by side for k=2 and heights h=1, 2, and 3: a root with two children, then two more levels of doubling, ending with eight leaves. Every internal node has exactly two children and all leaves sit at the same depth." width="100%"} Creates a tree where each internal node has exactly `k` children, with height `h`. The total number of nodes will be equal to `(k^(h+1) - 1) / (k - 1)` (or `h + 1` when `k=1`), and as in any tree there is one edge fewer than there are nodes. Nodes are created level by level (breadth-first): the root first, then its `k` children, then their children, and so on. Every edge joins a parent to one of its children, and in a directed graph it points from parent to child, so the root is the only node with no incoming edges. The tree is appended to the graph without touching or connecting to existing nodes. Balanced trees are useful for: - modeling hierarchies such as org charts, file systems, or taxonomies - generating test inputs for traversal, shortest-path, and tree algorithms with a known depth and branching structure - comparing network measures on a perfectly regular hierarchy The number of nodes grows exponentially with `h=`, so even moderate settings (say `k=4`, `h=10`, about 1.4 million nodes) get large quickly. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Branching factor: the number of children of every non-leaf node. Must be at least `1`; `k=1` produces a simple path of `h + 1` nodes. [h]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Height of the tree, i.e. the number of levels below the root (the root has height `0`). Must be non-negative; `h=0` adds only the root. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with a number given as a string, in breadth-first order and counting up from `count_nodes() + 1` at the time of the call (so the root is `"1"` in an empty graph, where the labels match the node IDs). If `False`, nodes are created without labels. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge, e.g. `"reports_to"`. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k=` is less than `1` or `h=` is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A balanced tree with branching factor `k` and height `h` has `(k^(h+1) - 1) / (k - 1)` nodes in total. A binary tree (`k=2`) of height `3` therefore has `1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15` nodes -- one root, two children, four grandchildren, and eight leaves: ::: {#449bbe4d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_balanced_tree(k=2, h=3) ) graph.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 15 ``` ::: ::: Because nodes are numbered breadth-first, a smaller tree makes the parent-child structure easy to read: node `"1"` is the root, `"2"` and `"3"` are its children, and `"4"` to `"7"` are the leaves. In a directed graph the edges point down the hierarchy: ::: {#b9f17062 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_balanced_tree(k=2, h=2) tree.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['1->2', '1->3', '2->4', '2->5', '3->6', '3->7'] ``` ::: ::: With `k=1`, every node has a single child, so the "tree" is just a path of `h + 1` nodes: ::: {#b8376128 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} chain = ec.Graph().add_balanced_tree(k=1, h=3) chain.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['1--2', '2--3', '3--4'] ``` ::: :::
